title: Local homotopy normal form at a good residue point
statement: Let $Y,Y'$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $P$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-derived-category] whose terms are finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $d,i,r\in\mathbb N$. Assume $P^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $n>d$. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism and $z\in Y'$. Suppose the termwise residue pullback $P_{g(z)}$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] has zero cohomology in all nonnegative degrees other than $i$ and finite locally free degree-$i$ cohomology of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq Y'$ of $z$ and a homotopy equivalence of cochain complexes between $(g^*P)|_U$ and the single complex on $\mathcal O_U^r$ in degree $i$. A homotopy equivalence consists of chain maps in both directions whose composites are chain homotopic to the identity.

proof.text: At the local ring at g(z), choose finite bases of the terms and repeatedly split a unit differential entry, using the chain-complex cancellation theorem with the integer indexing reversed. The bounded support gives finite total rank and each step decreases it by two, so the procedure terminates. The complement has only maximal-ideal entries in its differentials.

Reduction of the remaining complex modulo the maximal ideal has zero differential. Cancellation removes contractible summands, so preserves residue cohomology. In negative degrees the terms are zero by support; in nonnegative degrees the hypothesis says that the minimal remainder has r basis vectors in degree i and none elsewhere. Thus the local-ring complex is homotopy equivalent to the rank-r single complex.

The finitely many matrices for the basis changes, their inverses and contracting homotopies have entries in the local ring. Represent all entries on a common open neighbourhood and shrink until all finite matrix identities and invertibility relations hold. The stalks of the finite free terms outside the remaining degree are zero because their basis sizes are zero. Pull back this neighbourhood to Y\prime and pull back the explicit maps and homotopies termwise. They remain a homotopy equivalence on the inverse-image open U, which contains z.
